title: 10 Bollywood romantic movies that prove the '2000s were the best time for love
author: Saumya

There's never really a bad time to watch one of the many Bollywood romantic movies that the Hindi film industry became renowned for producing in the '2000s: a sound plot with a sweet/tragic love story at its centre, characters that were far from being cookie cutter, songs that remain memorable to this day—the perfect recipe for stomach butterflies. Streaming platforms may have us spoiled for choice, but back in the day, when any one of these movies was airing on television, you knew you were in for a good 4-5 hours of viewing (considering we lived in the blessed time of commercials). If you have a hankering for reexperiencing the good ol' days of Indian cinema, queue up any (or all) of these Bollywood romantic movies from a simpler time.

Mohabattein (2000)

Comprising a dynamic star cast of Amitabh Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, it comes as little surprise that Mohabattaein became the highest-grossing film the year it was released. And it only makes sense—23 years later, who doesn't like to watch repeated reruns of Raj Aryan (Shah Rukh Khan) challenging the archaic education system at Gurukul? With serene locations, blooming romances and well-timed dance sequences, Mohabattein never fails to enchant viewers with the acting and storyline, making it not only a critically acclaimed film but also one that leaves you humming its songs for a long time after you've watched it.

Kaho Naa… Pyaar Hai (2000)

Lovers who are destined to be together, cannot be parted by death—yes, that's a successful formula for a hit in Bollywood. Kaho Naa… Pyaar Hai marked the debuts of both Hrithik Roshan and Ameesha Patel, catapulting the former to instant heartthrob status for his rugged good looks and dancing skills. Although three hours long, this movie keeps you hooked throughout its run-time, thanks to the great acting chops, foot-tapping music, scenic locales and a solid plot about a love that endures even in the face of death.

Controversy often sells, and when it doesn't, it at least gets people talking. Filmmakers sometimes get accused of playing things safe compared to those who were active in the world of film during decades past, but this is an unfair broad criticism. Some filmmakers play it safe, sure, but others take risks and seem willing to stir up passionate opinions, be they positive or negative.

Some of the following films were intended to be controversial, some ended up controversial because they divided people, while others ended up provoking in ways both intended and unintended. What binds the following movies is the fact they were all released during the 2020s. You might not like them all, but you will likely feel some kind of way about them. They took risks, some of them offended people, and they all proved challenging in various (not to mention usually interesting) ways.

10 'The Apprentice' (2024)

Director: Ali Abbasi

The Apprentice is a gutsy film for many reasons, the most obvious being that it's a not-at-all flattering look at Donald Trump during the 1970s and '80s, with it getting a wide release about one month out from an election that will decide whether Trump becomes President again. The film itself is well-made, and the performances are fantastic, but it's been intrinsically linked to legal action and complications.

Nevertheless, this biographical movie still got released, and time will tell whether further legal issues spring up in its wake, especially if the people depicted in the movie view it as defamatory. Without picking a side, it's fair to observe that there are clear sides and a certain amount of division in America, and different people of different political beliefs are likely to react quite passionately to the content shown in The Apprentice. It's very bold in the places it goes; alarming and provocative are words that come to mind when watching it.

Dame Shirley Bassey

Let's take a look at other films that belong to the year 2000 and which turned 20 in 2020.

Mohabbatein

This romance drama will always be our favourite. Released in October of 2000, this movie revolves around students who come to study in a school named Gurukul, and end up falling in love. They face patriarchal beliefs and obstacles which make them question love as a concept in totality. Starring Amitabh Bachan, Shah Rukh Khan, Aishwarya Rai in the lead, this movie shows how love can conquer anything. 'Mohabbatein' became the longest running Chopra film in history.

Mission Kashmir

2000 also turned out to be the year for many patriotic films. Also, movies based on terrorism won hearts across the nation and worked best in cinema halls. 'Mission Kashmir' was one such film. This action-war was not just emotional but a tale of vengeance as well. Hritik Roshan and Sanjay Dutt played exceptional characters with the beautiful Preity Zinta playing Hrithik's childhood lover. With the direction and production of Vidhu Vinod Chopra, this intense plot won hearts.

Hera Pheri

'Hera Pheri' is a series of Indian comedy films that is one of the all-time-favourites on many. The first film was directed by Priyadarshan and produced by A.G. Nadiadwala.
